root_cause.text: The ALSA firewire-motu `hwdep_read()` DSP event copy loop incremented `consumed` in 4-byte chunks but failed to verify that `consumed + sizeof(ev)` stayed within the user-supplied `count`, allowing `put_user()` to write past the end of an unaligned user buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (put_user(ev, ptr))` to `if (consumed + sizeof(ev) > count || put_user(ev, ptr))`, and the commit message explicitly states that “when the user buffer size is not aligned to 4 bytes, it could overwrite beyond the buffer boundary.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check before copying hwdep events to user space to prevent writing past the requested buffer size.
intent_record.what: In the hwdep_read() loop, the conditional before writing each parsed event was changed from only checking put_user(ev, ptr) to first also checking whether consumed + sizeof(ev) exceeds count, and returning -EFAULT if either condition is true.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from attempting to copy a 32-bit event to user space when there is not enough remaining space in the caller's buffer, avoiding an out-of-bounds user write and ensuring the read operation fails safely instead of overrunning the requested count.

candidates.rationale: This increments the user-buffer offset by the event size without first ensuring that the full event still fits within count, so the loop can advance into a partial/unaligned final chunk and make the subsequent put_user() write past the requested buffer size.
This derives the user pointer from consumed even when the remaining space may be smaller than sizeof(ev), enabling put_user() to target memory beyond the user-supplied buffer on the final iteration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This computes the user-space write pointer from consumed without checking that a full event still fits in count, so the subsequent put_user() can write past the end of the requested buffer on a partial final chunk.

This advances the copy offset in fixed 4-byte increments without first verifying consumed + sizeof(ev) <= count, allowing the loop to progress into an unaligned partial buffer and trigger an out-of-bounds user write.

In the loop, it only checks `while (consumed < count && snd_motu_register_dsp_message_parser_copy_event(motu, &ev))`, then writes with `put_user(ev, ptr)` where `ptr = (u32 __user *)(buf + consumed)`, and increments `consumed += sizeof(ev);`.
